title: Payment Terms, Late Charges and Credit Hold Thresholds for Micro Market Settlements
content:
Credit terms on an Unattended Micro Market Program agreement are printed against the market format: the days a settlement invoice runs before it falls due, the monthly late percentage, the grace days before a late charge may be raised, the ceiling on the late charge raised against one invoice, and the days past due at which restocking stops.

| Market format | Payment terms, calendar days | Monthly late charge, per cent | Grace, calendar days | Late charge ceiling, USD | Restocking stops at days past due |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cooler & Snack Wall | 15 | 1.5 | 3 | 200 | 45 |
| Compact Micro Market | 21 | 1.5 | 5 | 450 | 60 |
| Standard Micro Market | 30 | 1.25 | 7 | 950 | 75 |
| Fresh Food Micro Market | 30 | 1.25 | 7 | 1800 | 90 |
| Expanded Campus Micro Market | 45 | 1 | 10 | 3400 | 90 |
| Smart Store Micro Market | 30 | 1.25 | 7 | 2400 | 75 |

## Reading the schedule

Three formats share payment terms of 30 calendar days: the Standard Micro Market, the Fresh Food Micro Market and the Smart Store Micro Market. Those same three share a monthly late percentage of 1.25 and a grace of 7 calendar days, and differ only in the ceiling on the late charge, at 950, 1800 and 2400 USD respectively.

The widest terms belong to the Expanded Campus Micro Market at 45 calendar days, with a grace of 10 calendar days, the lowest monthly late percentage at 1, and the highest ceiling on a single late charge at 3400 USD. The Cooler & Snack Wall takes the tightest terms of all at 15 calendar days, a grace of 3, and a ceiling of 200 USD, with restocking stopping at 45 days past due.
